verdict_text:
YES

The plan deletes exactly the 60 tensors of blocks 2, 6, 10, 14 (guarded by a count assert), then shifts the survivors in ascending order (3→2, 4→3, 5→4, 7→5, 8→6, 9→7, 11→8, 12→9, 13→10, 15→11) so every destination index is vacant at the moment of the move — no block overwrites a surviving one. The regexes are unambiguous: `layers\.3\.` cannot match `layers.13.` since the digit must follow `layers.` directly, and the delete alternation `(2|6|10|14)` followed by `\.` cannot match 12/13/15. Suffixes are preserved verbatim via the `\1` backreference, so names, values, shapes and dtypes are otherwise untouched and the 4 non-block tensors are left alone. All three required checks are present as asserts (no blocks 12–15, exactly 12 query_key_value weights, exactly 184 tensors = 244 − 60), and the output path matches `out/T1/model.safetensors`.
